title: SLO-prioritized yielding with KV hinting and GPU memory safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching must maximize throughput while meeting tenant-level latency SLOs and keeping KV cache and GPU memory within safe bounds. Current preemption is binary and causes oscillation for medium-priority tenants when GPUs experience transient KV pressure. Goal: implement an SLO-prioritized yielding mechanism that (1) differentiates soft vs hard preemption windows, (2) uses lightweight KV residency hints to avoid preempting requests that will hit the cache, and (3) enforces per-GPU memory safeguards ("memory sigils") to prevent OOM-caused broad evictions.

Proposed design summary:
- Soft-yield windows: admitTenant requests get per-tenant soft-yield credit buckets. When latency drift toward SLO threshold is detected, tenants draw from soft credits first; soft yielding temporarily reduces batch admission priority but allows requests to complete without full KV eviction.
- Hard preemption threshold: only applied when (a) projected 95th percentile latency will breach SLO within 200ms OR (b) GPU free memory falls below memory-sigil low-water mark. Hard preemption triggers immediate eviction of low-value slices.
- KV hinting: clients/routers attach a 2-bit KV hint per request: HOT (very likely resident), WARM (likely), COLD (unlikely), UNKNOWN. Router + runtime aggregate hints to avoid preempting HOT requests even under soft-yield staggers. Hints are best-effort and backward-compatible when missing.
- Memory sigils: per-GPU memory buckets with three tiers (GREEN/YELLOW/RED). Transitioning to RED enables aggressive cache compaction and increases hard-preempt aggressiveness; YELLOW biases toward soft-yield. Sigils computed from GPU free memory, per-tenant KV working set estimates, and kernel allocation pressure.
- Admission scoring: combine tenant SLO slack, soft-credit balance, KV-hint score, and sigil weight to compute an admission score. Lower scores are deferred or soft-yielded.

Trade-offs considered:
- Accuracy vs. complexity: KV hinting reduces unnecessary preempts but requires instrumentation in clients and routers. We keep hints optional to preserve compatibility.
- Soft-yield may increase tail latency for some low-priority tenants but reduces disruptive full preempts.
- Memory sigils add conservative heuristics; false positives will prefer soft-yield to avoid unnecessary evictions.

Implementation plan:
1) Wire a soft-credit accounting subsystem into the admission controller (2-week spike + 3-week implementation).
2) Add KV-hint fields to frontend router proto; implement hint aggregation at the edge (1-week).
3) Implement memory sigil sampler in the runtime agent with an API for scheduler (1-week spike + 2 weeks).
4) Build admission scorer combining signals and expose feature flag for gradual rollout.
5) Canary rollout: 1) internal dev cluster, 2) small set of low-risk tenants, 3) broader fleet with telemetry checks.

Observability and success criteria:
- Dashboards: per-tenant 50/95/99 latency, preemption count, soft-yield vs hard-preempt ratio, KV hit rate for hinted HOT requests, per-GPU memory sigil state.
- SLO regressions: no more than 1.2x increase in P95 for non-target tenants during canaries; target tenants maintain SLO within 5% of baseline.
- Cost: soft-yield should reduce unnecessary re-execution and reduce  p95 token-cost by at least 6% for mixed workloads.

Rollout kill-switch and fallback: feature flag default off. Rapid rollback path: disable scorer and fall back to current preemptor; runtime exposes quick toggles for sigil aggression levels.

Open questions:
- How to compute per-request KV residency probability server-side when clients cannot provide hints? (We plan to run a lightweight predictor in the router to guess residency using recent access histograms.)
- What are fair allocations for soft-credit replenishment rates per tenant tier? (Initial approach: proportional to reserved throughput with an anti-starvation floor.)

References and artifacts: Confluence design doc, benchmark spreadsheets, prototype PRs will be linked in comments below.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Spike notes: ran microbenchmarks on internal dev cluster. Soft-yield reduced hard preempts by ~42% under synthetic KV-churn workload. Prototype used deterministic HOT/COLD tags; adding UNKNOWN reduced misclassifications. - Aisha

2025-02-20 - Design review: PM (Marco Rivera) requested clarity on customer impact trade-offs. Action: add per-tenant opt-out and configurable soft-credit replenishment. Design accepted with minor changes. - Eleanor

2025-02-28 - Engineering update: implemented soft-credit ledger and basic scorer. Edge router proto change landed (github.com/redwood/edge-proto PR#412). Integration tests failing on memory-sigil sampling under low-frequency workloads; investigating sampling window size. - Eleanor

2025-03-05 - Performance: preliminary canary on dev-cluster shows P95 improved for best-effort tenants by 7% and P99 unchanged for target tenants. KV-hot hint accuracy at router ~87%. Need to instrument false-negative HOTs. - Aisha
2025-03-12 - Security/infra note: KMS not involved; no additional secrets. Confirmed security review not required by security (ticket SEC-874 closed). - Eleanor

2025-03-15 - Planning: schedule rollout gating dashboard with alerts: (a) tenant SLO delta > 5%, (b) hard-preempt spikes > 20% baseline, (c) per-GPU RED sigil time > 10%. Next steps: finalize sampler window and tune soft-credit replenishment. - Aisha
